messages.content: What is the historical significance of Heritage House?

**Heritage House (part of Dubai’s Heritage Village) matters because…**  

• It was set up in 1997 to **capture and showcase the traditional life of the UAE**, letting visitors see how people lived, worked, and celebrated in the past. (From Excerpt 1)  
• The site displays **old houses, handicrafts, and the customs of desert, marine, and mountain communities**, giving a hands‑on feel of heritage architecture. (From Excerpt 1)  
• Managed by the Dubai Culture & Arts Authority, it helps **preserve and promote local culture** for both residents and tourists. (From Excerpt 1 & Excerpt 3)

Hey! Here’s the quick low‑down on Dubai’s heritage spots and the classic “heritage house” vibe:  

• **Heritage Village** – opened in 1997 in the Al Shindagha Historical Neighborhood, right near the Diving Village (Excerpt 1).  
• It brings old‑school UAE life to life: wild, marine & mountain scenes, traditional houses, handicrafts, patterns, and daily customs (Excerpt 1).  
• Managed by the Dubai Culture & Arts Authority (Excerpt 1 & 2).  
• Opening times: Sun‑Thu 8:00‑22:00; Fri‑Sat 3:00‑22:00 (Excerpt 2).  

**Spotlight on a heritage house:**  

• Inside Al Fahidi Fort’s courtyard sits a traditional summer house called an **Arish** (Excerpt 3).  
• The Arish is built in the classic style and sits beside a bronze cannon, well, and boats, giving a real feel of historic living spaces (Excerpt 3).  

So, whether you wander the Heritage Village’s recreated streets or peek at the Arish at Al Fahidi Fort, you get a taste of Dubai’s old‑world architecture and culture. Enjoy exploring!
